title: Hidden Feelings
content:
For a few moments, Siddu remained silent.

His eyes stayed fixed on the mountains beyond the café window, but his mind was somewhere far away, trapped in memories he wished he could forget.

"When I heard the principal's warning..." he said softly, "...my anger knew no bounds."

He paused.

"I somehow controlled myself, walked back to my room, and spent the rest of the day trying to calm my mind."

The silence that followed lingered between them.

Sneha quietly observed Siddu's expression.

She could see that recalling those memories was becoming painful for him.

After a moment, she smiled gently.

"Siddu..."

He looked up.

"Hmm?"

"Shall we change the place for a while?"

A small smile appeared on his face.

"Yeah... sure."

Siddu looked relieved. For a while, both of them decided to leave the painful memories behind and simply enjoy the day.

After paying the bill, the two of them stepped out of the café.

The cool breeze of Shimla welcomed them once again.

They booked a cab to one of the famous viewpoints overlooking the mountains.

A few minutes later, the cab arrived.

Siddu got into the back seat first, and Sneha quietly sat beside him.

As the vehicle moved through the winding roads, silence once again settled between them.

This time...

It wasn't an uncomfortable silence.

It felt peaceful.

Sneha slowly turned her head and looked at Siddu.

The sunlight falling through the window gently illuminated his face.

He was looking outside, completely lost in thought.

Without realizing it, Sneha continued staring at him.

His calm face...

His thoughtful eyes...

Even the way he quietly admired the mountains...

Everything about him somehow made her heart feel lighter.

Just then, Siddu suddenly turned toward her.

Their eyes met.

Caught staring, Sneha immediately looked away.

A faint blush spread across her cheeks.

Siddu smiled.

"What happened?" he asked.

Sneha tried to act normal.

"Nothing."

A few seconds passed.

Then, pretending to sound casual, she asked,

"Can I ask you something?"

"Of course."

"How do I look?"

Siddu looked at her with a puzzled expression.

"Why are you asking me all of a sudden?"

Sneha shrugged with a small smile.

"Just... casually."

Siddu looked at her for a moment before answering honestly.

"Well..."

"I think your eyes are incredibly expressive."

"They're sharp... but at the same time, they carry a kindness that's hard to ignore."

He smiled softly.

"And your smile..."

"It has a way of making the people around you smile too."

He paused for a second before adding,

"To be honest... you're beautiful. Not just because of your looks, but because your kindness shows in everything you do."

Sneha's cheeks instantly turned red.

"Oh, stop it," she said shyly, gently hitting his arm.

Siddu laughed.

"I'm only telling the truth."

Soon, both of them burst into laughter, filling the cab with warmth that neither of them had expected.

As the laughter slowly faded, another thought quietly entered Sneha's mind.

Would Siddu... ever look at me the way I had begun to look at him?

The question surprised her.

She blinked.

Why did I even think that?

She quickly looked out of the window, trying to hide both her confusion and the blush that still remained on her face.

Within a few more minutes, the cab finally came to a stop.

They had reached one of Shimla's breathtaking viewpoints.

As they stepped out, a cool mountain breeze brushed past them.

The vast valley stretched endlessly before their eyes, covered with lush green hills and drifting clouds.

For a few moments, neither of them spoke.

They simply stood there, admiring the beauty of nature.

Then...

Siddu's phone suddenly rang.

He glanced at the screen.

The moment he saw the caller's name, a bright smile appeared on his face.

Sneha noticed the sudden change in his expression.

He answered the call.

"Hello."

For the next few moments, he listened quietly.

Then, with a smile that reflected both affection and certainty, he softly replied,

"How could I ever forget my love?"

Sneha froze.

The smile on her face slowly disappeared.

The words echoed inside her heart...

And for the first time since meeting Siddu...

She felt something she had never expected.

A quiet sting of jealousy.
